subject: Follow-up: Deployment mode and pricing — hosted vs dedicated vs private
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Chris Taylor <chris.taylor@finlytics.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-03-15T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: Deployment mode and pricing — hosted vs dedicated vs private

Hi Chris —

Great to meet you earlier. Quick recap from today's discovery and proposed next steps so we can align on deployment mode and costing:

Summary of your needs (as I understood them):
- High-throughput inference for document processing (~120 req/s average, spiking to ~400 req/s during batch runs)
- Strict data residency and encryption requirements for financial PII; preference toward VPC/private deployment if we can meet cost and ops constraints
- Want to support LLM-based extraction + reranking; model footprint likely Llama2-70B for highest quality, with smaller variants for cheaper fallbacks
- Timeline: pilot in Q2, production by end of Q3 if pricing and security are acceptable

Why this matters for deployment mode:
- Hosted API: fastest to onboard, usage-based per-token pricing, no infra ops for you, but may not meet strict residency/KMS requirements without Private options
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput and better per-token economics; good middle ground for consistent workloads with committed monthly spend
- Private VPC / on-prem: gives full control over networking/KMS and audit logs; higher setup and recurring platform licensing costs but required for regulated data

I've attached a preliminary pricing model (Finlytics_Redwood_Pricing_Model_20260315.xlsx) with ballpark numbers for each mode and a short SOC2 summary.

As next steps:
1) Can you confirm expected average qps and peak qps (you mentioned ~120 avg / 400 peak — please confirm)?
2) Clarify a rough monthly token volume (generations + embeddings) or examples of batch sizes so we can model per-token vs reserved capacity economics
3) Would your security/compliance team require an on-prem deployment or will VPC with KMS/HSM and SOC2+ contractual terms be enough?

If helpful, we can do a short pricing sync next week (30 min) to walk the spreadsheet and tradeoffs (per-token hosted vs committed dedicated vs Private one-time onboarding + monthly license).

Thanks —
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | (415) 555-0123

Date: 2026-03-16T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Deployment mode and pricing — hosted vs dedicated vs private

Thanks Marissa — good summary. A few clarifications from our side:

- QPS: 120 req/s average is correct for our steady-state processing. During runbooks (end of month processing) we hit short spikes to ~400 req/s for ~20–30 minute windows.
- Models: primary is Llama2-70B for extraction; we can evaluate Mistral/7B for lower-cost paths. Latency targets: p95 < 300ms for interactive pieces, batch can be higher.
- Data residency: we need data to stay in our AWS VPC in us-west-2. KMS integration is essential. If Private VPC meets that without onerous infra burden on our side, that would be ideal. If not, Dedicated within us-west-2 with dedicated networking and KMS integration could work.
- Tokens: hard to estimate exactly, but rough monthly generation tokens ~1.2B tokens, embeddings ~500M tokens (for search + rerank).

On pricing structure:
- We're keen to understand the crossover point where dedicated/reserved commits become cheaper than hosted per-token.
- We prefer multi-month commits if it yields meaningful discounts but need visibility into minimum commit size and exit terms.

Can you run the cost model with these volumes and come back with a 3-month pilot and a 12-month committed option (with committed spend and estimated unit economics)? Also include the upfront onboarding/one-time work for Private (if applicable).

I'll loop in our security lead if you need more detail on KMS/SOC2 requirements.

—Chris

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2026-03-16T15:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Deployment mode and pricing — hosted vs dedicated vs private

Thanks Chris — super helpful detail. I ran a quick set of ballpark models (see attached spreadsheet). Highlights and assumptions:

Assumptions
- Monthly tokens: 1.2B generation tokens, 0.5B embedding tokens
- Typical generation prompt+completion avg tokens: 220 tokens per request
- Peak capacity handled via autoscaling/burst in Dedicated; spikes short enough that we model burstable capacity rather than constant extra headroom

Hosted API (pay-as-you-go) — quick math
- Generation avg unit price: $0.00060 / token (example for Llama2-70B verified model)
- Embeddings avg unit price: $0.00005 / token
- Estimated monthly cost: generation ~ $720k, embeddings ~ $25k => total ~ $745k/month
- Pros: no infra ops, fastest to market. Cons: unit costs highest, limited control over private networking/KMS unless paired with Private enterprise terms

Dedicated (reserved capacity) — quick math
- Example: reserved 8x A100-style GPU pool with autoscale and hot standby for spikes
- Platform + infra blended rate (after typical committed discount): ~$40k–$60k per GPU/month depending on model and quantization profile
- For Llama2-70B inference, estimated baseline monthly: $120k–$240k (for a pool sized to meet your steady-state throughput), plus tokenization overhead and storage.
- With a 3-month reserved commit at $60k/GPU/month and a 20% commit discount, estimated: ~ $192k/month effective for the pool (example).
- Pros: much better unit economics at scale, predictable throughput, can integrate with VPC peering and customer KMS in many configurations

Private VPC / On-prem
- One-time onboarding & setup: typically $40k–$120k depending on network, HSM/KMS integration, and audit requirements; recurring platform license + infra costs (negotiated enterprise terms).
- If you require on-prem hardware, we'd coordinate sizing with your infra team; Opex likely comparable to dedicated but with additional platform license fees.
- Pros: meets strict residency/KMS + audit controls. Cons: higher init cost and longer lead time.

Recommended next steps
1) We can prepare a formal 3-month pilot offer (committed spend + discounted dedicated pool) vs hosted per-token estimate. Example options to include in the offer:
   - 3-month pilot: commit to ~$180k/month reserved (example) — 15–20% discount vs list dedicated rates; Redwood handles capacity and SLA for that pool.
   - 12-month committed: progressive discounts (20–30%) with more favorable on-call and onboarding support.
2) For Private: estimate an onboarding SOW once you confirm whether VPC-only (Redwood-managed control plane) or full on-prem is needed.
3) I'll schedule a 30-min pricing walk-through early next week — please share 2 windows that work.

I've attached the spreadsheet with line-item math (Finlytics_Redwood_Pricing_Model_20260315.xlsx) and the SOC2 summary. Aditya (cc'd) can jump on the pricing call to go deeper into GPU sizing and quantization tradeoffs.

—Marissa

Thanks Marissa — this is exactly what we needed to decide next steps. A few quick notes:

- We'd like a formal 3-month pilot proposal and a 12-month committed option to review with finance. Please include minimum commit, break clauses, and estimated SLA credits.
- Security: please send the SOC2 and a short note on KMS/HSM options (which KMS providers do you integrate with? we use AWS KMS in us-west-2). Also share the typical SOW range for Private VPC onboarding if we go that route.
- Availability: I'm available Mon 2026-03-22 10:00–11:00 PT or Tue 2026-03-23 14:00–15:00 PT for the pricing sync.

Looping in Aisha (security) and our procurement lead to coordinate contract/legal questions.
